These outlets claimed Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 authorizes tariffs in response to trade deficits and permits them for 150 days without mentioning the statutory requirement that tariffs address "large and serious balance-of-payments deficits." Popular Information documents that the U.S. has a zero balance-of-payments deficit, rendering Trump's invocation legally baseless.
events.why_relevant: Systematic misreporting of statutory law by major news outlets creates public misunderstanding of presidential authority and undermines informed democratic scrutiny of executive power.
events.basis: Several prominent outlets falsely reported that the Trade Act gives Trump the legal authority to impose temporary tariffs of up to 15% in response to trade deficits.

events.summary: A survey of approximately 6,000 CFOs, CEOs, and executives across the U.S., UK, Germany, and Australia found that around 70 percent of firms actively use AI. While firms reported little impact over the prior three years, they forecast sizable impacts over the next three years, predicting AI will boost productivity by 1.4 percent, increase output by 0.8 percent, and cut employment by 0.7 percent. However, surveyed employees predicted a 0.5 percent increase in employment from AI, creating a significant gap between senior executive and worker expectations.
events.why_relevant: Divergence between executive and worker expectations on AI employment effects signals potential labor market disruption and worker anxiety that may affect policy and social stability.
events.federal_nexus: survey spans multiple countries including the U.S.
events.basis: Firms predict sizable impacts over the next 3 years, forecasting AI will boost productivity by 1.4%, increase output by 0.8% and cut employment by 0.7%. We also survey individual employees who predict a 0.5% increase in employment in the next 3 years as a result of AI.

events.title: DOJ appears to have illegally withheld material from Epstein files
events.summary: NPR reporter Stephen Fowler reported on Tuesday morning that the Department of Justice appears to have illegally withheld material from the Epstein files. The withheld material relates to allegations that Trump sexually assaulted two girls when they were approximately thirteen years old. The DOJ also removed from published files documents mentioning Trump among allegations against convicted sexual abuser Epstein. On February 14, Attorney General Pam Bondi and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche told Congress they had not withheld or redacted records "on the basis of embarrassment, reputational harm, or political sensitivity." The Epstein Files Transparency Act, which required release of all files by December 19, 2025, prohibits such redactions except to protect victims and survivors.
events.why_relevant: The withholding of material from a congressionally mandated transparency release violates statutory requirements and suggests use of prosecutorial discretion to shield the president from public scrutiny.
events.basis: On Tuesday morning, Stephen Fowler of NPR built on earlier reporting by independent journalist Roger Sollenberger to report that the Department of Justice (DOJ) appears to have illegally withheld material from the Epstein files. That material is related to allegations that Trump sexually assaulted two girls when they were about thirteen years old.

events.title: DOJ removed and restored Epstein-related photograph from public website
events.summary: The Department of Justice removed a photograph from its Epstein files website showing Trump appointee Howard Lutnick with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein on Epstein's island. The photo had been archived by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine on January 31 and was later removed, returning a "Page not found" error. Within hours of CBS News publishing a story about the removal, DOJ restored the photograph. DOJ later stated the removal was due to the image being "part of a batch of files that had been flagged for nudity."
events.why_relevant: The temporary removal of a publicly released document from official government records raises questions about document control, the timing of removal relative to media scrutiny, and the adequacy of the stated justification for suppressing evidence related to a sitting president's associations.
events.basis: A photo released last month by DOJ as part of the Epstein files that showed Howard Lutnick with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein on Epstein's island in the Caribbean was removed from DOJ's website before being restored Thursday night.

events.title: Oman's Foreign Minister announced Iran had agreed to nuclear verification framework hours before strikes
events.summary: On Friday, February 27, less than 24 hours before the first bombs hit Tehran, Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi went public with an unusually specific description of a framework he said the parties had reached in recent talks. Albusaidi said Iran had agreed to never stockpile enriched uranium or nuclear material and to accept full IAEA verification, calling it a breakthrough "never achieved" before. He said all remaining issues could be resolved within months and that a deal was "within reach." Additional talks were scheduled in Vienna for the following Monday. Albusaidi flew to Washington on Friday to brief U.S. officials and appeared on CBS television with his message. Trita Parsi of the Quincy Institute noted publicly that Albusaidi going on U.S. television was unusually direct, suggesting it was meant to make clear to the American public that diplomacy was still producing results when the administration chose war instead.
events.why_relevant: Active diplomatic negotiations producing reported breakthroughs on nuclear verification were abandoned within hours in favor of military action, raising questions about whether military escalation was chosen despite viable diplomatic alternatives.
events.basis: Albusaidi said Iran had agreed to never stockpile enriched uranium or nuclear material and to accept full IAEA verification calling it a breakthrough 'never achieved' before. Additional talks were scheduled in Vienna for the following week.

events.title: US military uses laser to down CBP drone near Mexico border, disrupting airspace
events.summary: On Thursday 27 February, the US military deployed a high-energy laser system to shoot down an unmanned aerial system it believed was a threat near Fort Hancock on the US-Mexico border in Texas. The drone turned out to belong to US Customs and Border Protection. Airspace around Fort Hancock was closed as a result. This was the second such incident in two weeks; an earlier incident on 11 February involved CBP deploying a laser against what was thought to be a cartel drone but was actually a party balloon, causing the FAA to shut down El Paso airspace for 10 days before lifting the order after 8 hours.
events.why_relevant: The incident reveals dangerous lack of coordination between federal agencies (Pentagon, CBP, FAA) and raises questions about military deployment of weapons systems and civilian airspace safety, prompting Democratic calls for investigation and bipartisan coordination legislation.
